text: You've seen this crest a thousand times. But do you know what every piece of it means?
Top left: a red cross on a white field.
People often ask why Barsa put England's flag on their badge. It has nothing to do with England.
It's the Cross of Saint George, Sant Jordee in Catalan: the patron saint of Catalonia, the knight who slays the dragon in the legend.
Every April 23rd, on Sant Jordee's Day, people in Barcelona give each other roses and books.
Top right: red stripes on gold.
That's the Sen-yera, the flag of Catalonia. It goes back to the Counts of Barcelona and the medieval Crown of Aragon.
That's why Barsa captains wear its colours on the armband, and why the stands are full of it.
At the bottom: blue and garnet stripes. Blow-grana.
Joan Gamper, a Swiss footballer, founded the club in eighteen ninety-nine. One popular story says he took the colours from his old club, FC Basel.
And right in the middle, an old leather ball, because it all started with a love of the game.
The design was chosen in a nineteen-ten competition. The winner was Carles Comma-mala, a medical student who also played for Barsa.
So next time you see it, remember: a saint, a homeland, a club, and a ball. Visca Barsa!
